data.title: Merck, Isomorphic Labs Enter Strategic Research Collaboration
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Merck will collaborate with Isomorphic Labs, an AI-first drug design company, to develop new therapies.

The companies on Thursday said they will collaborate to discover therapeutic small-molecule candidates against an oncology target of strategic importance.

Isomorphic Labs will deliver molecular designs derived from its artificial-intelligence-enabled drug design engine.

Meanwhile, Merck will provide data sets on which the drug design engine will run. It will additionally be responsible for preclinical and clinical development, as well as manufacturing and commercialization of any products derived from the collaboration.

"By combining Merck's substantial internal data capabilities and discovery expertise with Isomorphic Labs' powerful modeling and compute capabilities, we aim to identify new ways to design and create better candidates faster," said George Addona, head of discovery for preclinical development and translational medicine at Merck Research Laboratories.

Under the terms of the agreement, Isomorphic Labs will receive an undisclosed, upfront payment from Merck.

Isomorphic Labs will additionally be eligible for payments based on the achievement of specified research, development, regulatory and commercial milestones, as well as tiered royalties on net sales. It will also receive an option to co-fund development activities, in return for elevated royalties.

data.title: Marsh’s Oliver Wyman to Acquire Financial Services and Technology Consultancy Synpulse
data.description:
Marsh’s Oliver Wyman to Acquire Financial Services and Technology Consultancy Synpulse

Oliver Wyman, a global leader in management consulting and a Marsh business (NYSE:MRSH), today announced an agreement to acquire Synpulse, a global technology consulting and AI platform company serving banks, insurers, wealth managers and other financial services organizations. Terms of the deal, expected to close in early 2027, were not disclosed.

Banks, insurers and asset managers face significant changes driven by advances in technology, data and AI, as well as evolving business models. As these changes accelerate, clients are looking for partners who can help them navigate every stage of transformation, from strategy to technology implementation and execution. Oliver Wyman and Synpulse have already been working together with combined teams on multiple end-to-end transformations for our clients. The acquisition will enable the two businesses to continue to work closely together, combining complementary capabilities and teams to service clients across strategy, technology and implementation.

Synpulse brings technology experience that helps financial institutions modernize legacy systems, improve operations and respond to changing client needs. Through responsible AI strategy and digital ecosystem transformation, Synpulse helps clients bring new products to market faster, simplify operations, and deliver more personalized customer experiences.

“Our clients don’t separate strategy from technology and execution—they need great ideas to deliver real change,” said Ted Moynihan, President and CEO of Oliver Wyman and Marsh Management Consulting. “Synpulse brings exceptional technology consulting and AI engineering capabilities, deep financial services expertise and a track record of delivering complex enterprise change. Together, we will deliver a winning combination of talent and technology to help clients achieve their biggest ambitions.”

“Since our founding in 1996, Synpulse has built a strong position as a trusted partner to financial institutions in their digital transformations,” said Konrad Niggli, Co-CEO of Synpulse. "Working alongside Oliver Wyman will enable us to support our clients across the entire digital and AI transformation journey, from strategy through implementation and execution. It gives us greater scale to deepen the value we bring to our clients.”

“Bringing our teams together creates opportunities to expand our reach across markets, take on larger and more complex transformation projects, and accelerate our growth across regions. It also strengthens our ability to invest in AI and technology, further enhancing the capabilities we bring to our clients,” said Yves Roesti, Co-CEO of Synpulse.

Upon closing, Synpulse’s approximately 1,200 employees will continue to operate from offices in North America, Europe and Asia. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

About Oliver Wyman Oliver Wyman is a business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit oliverwyman.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

About Synpulse Synpulse is a global consulting and technology company specializing in financial services. Its teams work with banks, insurers, wealth managers and other financial institutions across strategy, design, technology implementation and operations. Combining financial services expertise with technology, Synpulse works with its technology division Synpulse8 and a network of more than 100 ecosystem partners to support clients from strategy through implementation. Around 1,200 Synpulse professionals work across more than 20 locations worldwide. For more information visit synpulse.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

data.title: With Musical Short "PAPmusic Game Out of Every Box": LeiKiè Unveils Two Game Modes, PAPcrazy and PAPrhythm
data.description:
With Musical Short "PAPmusic Game Out of Every Box": LeiKiè Unveils Two Game Modes, PAPcrazy and PAPrhythm

With Musical Short "PAPmusic Game Out of Every Box": LeiKiè Unveils Two Game Modes, PAPcrazy and PAPrhythm

PR Newswire

MILAN, Nov. 19, 2026

The fourth and final musical chapter wraps up a story of clues and revelations. Pre-registration is open on Google Play.

MILAN, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LeiKiè unveils PAPcrazy and PAPrhythm, two game modes of PAPgame, the mobile video game developed and published by Not Just Music S.r.l. for Android and iOS, now open for Pre-registration on Google Play

With her fourth single, released in English as "PAPmusic Game Out of Every Box" and in Italian as "PAPmusic Game Fuori dagli Schemi", LeiKiè concludes the musical storytelling journey behind the game.

Think you've figured out PAPgame? Think outside the box—again!

Watch now the video: https://youtu.be/OgSet_lnhjE

The new musical short film reveals another surprise: music doesn't just accompany the game. Music becomes the game!

TWO WAYS TO PLAY. ONE PAPWORLD.

PAPworld characters and objects take center stage to introduce PAPrhythm, the new rhythm-game experience alongside PAPcrazy, the first-person adventure set in Milan's Piazza Duomo.

At launch, the PAPshop will offer around 50 songs usable in both experiences: some gifted, some available for purchase and others earned through gameplay. In PAPrhythm, players win rewards by taking on individual songs; in PAPcrazy, they complete challenges to collect 11 trophies—and can win them again and again.

WIN. RESTART. WIN AGAIN!

In PAPcrazy, six weather-themed environments span 35 PAPranks. On the first playthrough, each environment rewards players with a song: six free tracks earned through gameplay. Beyond them, another stage leads to the final Never-Ending PAPstory trophy, spreading PAPlove across Piazza Duomo.

"Thinking outside the box is the spirit of PAPmusic: even when one chapter ends, the Never-Ending PAPstory goes on!" says PAPgame creator LeiKiè.

But victory isn't the end! Inspired by a prestige loop, the cyclical progression system lets players restart while keeping their score, reclaim trophies and record the number of wins on each one. Subsequent cycles bring different gifts between environments. PAPcoins and PAPgems accompany the adventure.

FOUR MUSICAL SHORT FILMS. ONE MYSTERY UNFOLDING.

PAPgame's story has been told through four musical shorts, each revealing new clues. "BREAKING PAPnews" sparked the mystery in June; "I Play PAPmusic Game" revealed in July that it was a video game; "Is it Just a Game?" brought more questions and PAPsurprises in September. Now "PAPmusic Game Out of Every Box" completes the journey with a playable revelation.

The first three campaigns generated approximately 50 million social media views and 5,500 international media publications.

Not Just Music S.r.l. is the Italian production company behind the movie PAPmusic – Animation for Fashion and the videogame PAPgame. Bringing together animation, original music, fashion and interactive entertainment, the company develops and produces creative projects across film, music and gaming. Not Just Music is both developer and publisher of PAPgame for Android and iOS.

AND NOW?

With all four musical chapters concluded, how can a Never-Ending PAPstory ever end? The next PAPnews might bring even more surprises...

data.title: Europe Has 'Zero Interest' in Resuming Russian Gas Imports, U.S. Energy Chief Says
data.description:
By Adam Whittaker

European nations don't want to restart imports of Russian gas, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said.

"I've heard zero interest in going back," Wright said in reference to Europe resuming energy imports. He was speaking to the press at the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation conference in Poland on Thursday.

The continent previously suffered from its reliance on Russian gas and is vocally resistant to resuming imports after they are phased out, Wright said.

Europe has been weaning itself off Russian energy imports since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine early in 2022. European Union legislation states that all purchases of Russian natural gas must be phased out by the end of 2027, and European leaders have opposed the full resumption of imports from a country they view as a strategic threat.

The Wall Street Journal reported earlier this month that a plan, broached by U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff during trips to Moscow and Kyiv in September, would see Russian gas sold into Europe via a U.S. intermediary. The plan was later put on the back burner, but the potential for Russian gas to return to Europe hangs over the continent, the Journal reported.

data.title: Walmart Raises Fiscal Year Guidance Amid 3Q Earnings Beat
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Walmart posted fiscal third-quarter results that exceeded Wall Street's expectations, and the retail giant once again raised its full-year guidance.

Walmart on Thursday reported adjusted earnings of 65 cents a share for the quarter ended Oct. 31, up from 62 cents a share a year earlier and ahead of the 64 cents a share that analysts polled by FactSet, on average, had been expecting.

Revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8 billion, topping the $187.4 billion that analysts were looking for.

The Bentonville, Ark., company said now expects full-year adjusted earnings of $2.84 to $2.89 a share, up from its increased August forecast of $2.80 to $2.87 a share. Wall Street has already penciled in a full-year profit of $2.89 a share.

Walmart also raised its forecast for full-year constant-currency sales growth to 4.9% to 5.2% from a prior range of 4% to 5%.

Did You Lose Money Investing in Portillo's Inc. (PTLO)? Robbins LLP Urges Investors with Large Losses to Contact the Firm About Their Rights

Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP reminds investors it has filed a class action lawsuit on behalf of all purchasers of Portillo's Inc. ("Portillo's") (NASDAQ: PTLO) common stock between September 19, 2023 and May 4, 2026, inclusive (the "Class Period"). The complaint, filed in the Northern District of Illinois, alleges violations of sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Rule 10b-5, promulgated thereunder. The complaint seeks relief on behalf of the named plaintiff and all other similarly situated holders of Portillo's during the Class Period. The named plaintiff is represented by Robbins LLP.

What Does the Complaint Allege?

Portillo's is a fast-casual restaurant chain that specializes in Chicago-style food, such as Italian beef sandwiches and Chicago-style hot dogs and sausages.

The Portillo's class action lawsuit alleges that throughout the Class Period, Defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (i) Portillo's rapid expansion was going poorly, as it overbuilt in areas without any name recognition, cannibalized its own stores, and marketing could not drive enough additional interest to justify the expansion; (ii) the Company was having to offer promotions to drive interest, which was decreasing same-restaurant sales; and (iii) as a result of the foregoing, Defendants' positive statements about the Company's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

The truth of Portillo's deficiencies came to light through a series of partial disclosures between August 4, 2025 and May 5, 2026, when the Company finally revealed it had expanded too quickly in markets where awareness and demand were insufficient, placed restaurants too close together, cannibalized demand, incurred millions of dollars in dead-site and strategic-reset costs, and ultimately adopted a slower and more disciplined development strategy.

On this news, the price of Portillo's common stock dropped precipitously from $5.72 per share when the market closed on May 4, 2026, to $4.79 per share when the market closed on May 5, 2026, a drop of 16.3%. The Company's stock continued to fall over the following trading days and closed at just $3.93 per share on May 18, 2026, a total drop of $1.79 per share, or 31.2%, on unusually high trading volume.

Next Steps: If you purchased or otherwise acquired Portillo's, Inc. common stock between September 19, 2023 and May 4, 2026, and wish to serve as lead plaintiff, you have up to January 11, 2027, to ask the court to appoint you as the lead plaintiff for the class.

If you wish to discuss this action or have any questions concerning this notice or your rights or interests, please contact attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr. of Robbins LLP at (800) 350-6003, via email, or via the shareholder information form on our website. Any member of the class may move the Court to serve as lead plaintiff through counsel of their choice or may choose to do nothing and remain an absent class member. A copy of the complaint can be found here.

All representation is on a contingency fee basis. Shareholders pay no fees or expenses.

data.title: Equinor Continues Work to Halt Cyberattack
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Equinor said that a cyberattack detected on Tuesday is continuing, but added that production is running as normal and there are no indications that data has been stolen or altered.

The Norwegian energy company previously reported that an attack on certain IT systems had been identified, adding that it isn't a virus attack, so there is no chance of it spreading.

The company is in talks with national security authorities, and the police have been notified.

In an update Thursday, the company said that the attack does not appear to be specifically targeting Equinor, and that work to stop it and restore full integrity to affected systems continues.

"It is too early to say how long this work will take," it said.

data.title: Deutsche Bank got its dollar call for 2026 wrong. Why it's shifting tack now.
data.description:
By Jules Rimmer

Don't bet against the dollar yet; U.S. growth is stronger and its bond yields are higher.

The AI boom has been tremendously supportive of the dollar

Deutsche Bank was bearish on the dollar for 2026. It was the wrong call. The dollar index has risen 5.4% so far this year, not a huge move by historical standards but confounding many forecasts of the end of U.S. exceptionalism. Now, for 2027, Deutsche Bank has changed its view and predicts a "Superdollar," although "AI dollar" seems more appropriate.

The continuation of U.S. exceptionalism has forced Deutsche Bank's forex strategists Tim Baker, George Saravelos, Mallika Sachdeva and Charlie Hyams to revise their dollar DXY forecasts higher for 2027. These new targets are set out in a 2027 outlook piece dispatched to clients Thursday.

By the end of next year they predict the euro (EURUSD) at $1.15, the dollar to trade at 145 yen (USDJPY), for the British pound (GBPUSD) to be at $1.32 and for each Canadian dollar (CADUSD) to buy 0.83 U.S. greenbacks.

Those four currencies account for 90% of the DXY basket. The stronger yen is largely offset by a weaker euro.

Since its February low, the dollar has increased more than 7%. The AI boom, Baker writes, is largely responsible. It's pushed real rates higher, attracted huge equity inflows, exerted upward pressure on inflation and that in turn has turned the Fed more hawkish. "The AI dollar is alive and well," the report notes.

US economic outperformance is driven by robust capex spending

Baker and team now anticipate a "higher for longer" dollar in the first half of next year. This argument is supported by the U.S. topping the rankings for government bond yields and economic growth, as well as persistent equity inflows. This yield advantage is crucial in attracting international capital flows, especially from Asian countries recycling their immense trade surpluses.

The USD is hanging around high-yielder status - not an environment in which the dollar tends to fall

What might cause the weakening in the dollar that Deutsche Bank foresees in the second half of 2027? A slowdown in the AI boom, and a downgrading of capex expectations. That would lower bond yields and reduce equity inflows. Downside risks to energy prices from a potential resolution of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine could also contribute to dollar weakness. Further out, Baker and team worry about the large twin deficit the U.S. government operates.

Outside the U.S. Baker sees a difficult environment for the euro, especially given the political tribulations experienced in France, but he reckons much of the French risk premium is already priced in. Prospects for the euro should improve in the second half of the year.

In Asia, the report identifies plenty of scope for outperformance given those booming regional trade surpluses with the U.S. and their recycling into U.S. assets. Baker expects capital repatriation, Bank of Japan tightening and higher domestic yields to push the yen almost 10% higher in 2027.

-Jules Rimmer

data.title: FHLBank Chicago Invests $5.6 Million to Expand Housing Counseling Across Illinois and Wisconsin
data.description:
FHLBank Chicago Invests $5.6 Million to Expand Housing Counseling Across Illinois and Wisconsin

2026 investment builds on more than $13 million awarded since 2022 to expand housing counseling

The Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago (FHLBank Chicago) is providing $5.6 million in 2026 funding through its Community First® Housing Counseling Resource Program (HCRP) to expand access to housing counseling services across Illinois and Wisconsin. The 2026 funding supports the Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA) and the Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority (WHEDA), which work with networks of U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)-certified housing counseling agencies in their respective states.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119963953/en/

From left: Kristin Faust, Executive Director of the Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA); Katie Naftzger, Senior Vice President and Community Investment Officer at FHLBank Chicago; and Elmer Moore Jr., Executive Director and CEO of the Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority (WHEDA), celebrate FHLBank Chicago’s $5.6 million investment in its Community First® Housing Counseling Resource Program (HCRP).

“Housing counseling can be an important first step toward sustainable homeownership,” said Katie Naftzger, Senior Vice President and Community Investment Officer at FHLBank Chicago. “Through our partnerships with IHDA and WHEDA, we're helping more families prepare for homeownership while strengthening connections between housing counseling agencies and our member financial institutions.”

Launched in 2022, the HCRP expands access to financial education, credit preparation, and homebuyer support services. The program also supports current homeowners with post-purchase education and foreclosure prevention counseling. IHDA and WHEDA administer the program in their respective states, awarding grants to HUD-certified housing counseling agencies to expand their capacity to serve households.

Through the end of 2025, FHLBank Chicago has awarded more than $13 million through the HCRP, with participating housing counseling agencies serving more than 105,000 households across Illinois and Wisconsin. Nearly 9,000 of those households achieved homeownership.

“Homeownership is one of the most powerful tools for building equity and securing a long-term future, but for too many, it can feel increasingly out of reach,” said IHDA Executive Director Kristin Faust. “Through our partnership with FHLBank Chicago, we are helping first-time buyers overcome barriers to homeownership through housing counseling, financial literacy, and credit preparation. This direct support gives more families the guidance and resources they need to make informed decisions and build a strong foundation for sustainable homeownership.”

“Housing counseling agencies are essential to expanding homeownership opportunities across Wisconsin,” said Elmer Moore Jr., Executive Director and CEO of WHEDA. “Our continued partnership with FHLBank Chicago strengthens the capacity of these organizations to serve more households, expand their reach across the state and provide the resources families need to prepare for sustainable homeownership.”

The HCRP also strengthens connections between HUD-certified housing counseling agencies and FHLBank Chicago member financial institutions, helping connect mortgage-ready homebuyers with financing and other resources. These include FHLBank Chicago's Downpayment Plus® Program, which provides eligible homebuyers with down payment and closing cost assistance through participating members.

To learn more about the HCRP and view supported housing counseling agencies across Illinois and Wisconsin, visit the Housing Counseling Resource Program webpage.

About the Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago

FHLBank Chicago is a regional bank in the Federal Home Loan Bank System. FHLBanks are government-sponsored enterprises created by Congress to ensure access to low-cost funding for their member financial institutions, with a focus on providing solutions that support the housing and community development needs of members’ customers. FHLBank Chicago is a self-capitalizing cooperative, owned by its Illinois and Wisconsin members, including commercial banks, credit unions, insurance companies, savings institutions and community development financial institutions. To learn more about FHLBank Chicago, please visit fhlbc.com.

Community First® is a registered trademark of the Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago.
